To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the students' experiences of causing pain were characterized by the following themes: (a) feeling the pain of another person, (b) the pain caused, (c) the student's own suffering, and (d) the student's suffering as a consequence of the pain caused; 2) the strategies for dealing with pain were: (a) the need to be prepared, (b) putting yourself in the other's place, (c) trying to forget the pain caused

1) the majority of students (60%) reported having had an experience in which they caused pain to a patient, 2) students reported that the most common cause of pain was a procedure, 3) most students (80%) had a negative reaction to the pain they caused, 4) the most common reaction was feeling guilty, and 5) students felt that the pain they caused was not justified.
